chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about something regarding divorce, so he said: 'When a man divorces his wife with a divorce in which he does not have the right of return (ba'in), she becomes separated from him at the moment he divorces her, she owns herself, and he has no authority over her; she may go wherever she wishes, and she has no maintenance (nafaqah) due from him.'
I said: 'Is it not that Allah says:
"Do not expel them from their homes, nor should they [themselves] leave."

He said: 'He meant by that the one who is divorced with a revocable divorce after a revocable divorce (i.e., the first or second divorce before the third). That is the one who is not expelled and does not leave until she is divorced a third time. When she is divorced a third time, she becomes separated from him and has no maintenance. And the woman whom the man divorces with one divorce, then leaves her until her waiting period (ajal) elapses (i.e., the final irrevocable divorce), this one also observes her waiting period in her husband's house, and she has maintenance and residence until her waiting period ends.'

As for maintenance, it remains obligatory on the husband as long as he has the right of return over her. When she becomes separated and the bond of marriage is severed between them, she has no inheritance [from him], and we have already mentioned that. And to add clarification to this is what was narrated:

key_terms.الرَّجْعَة: Right of return (revocability during the waiting period)
key_terms.السُّكْنَى: Residence (right to live in the marital home)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on maintenance and residence for a wife in an irrevocable divorce (ba'in) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) elucidates the legal distinction between a revocable divorce, where the wife retains residence and maintenance during the 'iddah, and an irrevocable divorce (ba'in), where she immediately gains autonomy and is not entitled to maintenance. This narration highlights the Shia jurisprudential understanding that the Quranic command 'do not expel them' (65:1) specifically applies to the period of revocability, whereas the final third divorce severs the bond completely. The Imam further clarifies that maintenance is tied to the husband's right of return, reinforcing the link between marital status and financial obligations.
